# Sprains and strains

Notes from the physical therapist after the ankle injury.

## The first 48 hours

For the first two days rest the joint, ice it for 15 to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours, wrap it with an elastic bandage, and raise it above heart level. Do not apply heat, and avoid alcohol and hot baths, because heat increases swelling.

## After the first few days

From about day 3, once the swelling has stopped growing, the joint can be warmed and moved. Use a heating pad or a warm soak for 15 to 20 minutes before gentle stretching and range-of-motion exercises, then ice again afterward if it swells. Walking on the ankle as pain allows speeds recovery more than keeping it still. A moderate sprain takes 2 to 6 weeks to settle.

## When to get an X-ray

Get it checked if you cannot take four steps, if the bone itself is tender, if the foot is numb or looks out of shape, or if there is no improvement after a week.

## Wraps and braces

An elastic wrap should be snug, not tight: take it off if the toes go numb, blue or cold. A lace-up brace protects the ankle on uneven ground while it heals.

## Back strain

Staying gently active heals a strained back faster than bed rest. Use heat for tight muscles, avoid heavy lifting for a few weeks, and see a doctor for numbness, weakness in a leg, or loss of bladder control.
